g.text: No external resistors — the inputs use the
A straight key uses only Tip + Sleeve.
The LED is on the board (GPIO21) — no wiring.
CHG LED → D3 — optional charge sense,
− is the pad nearer the USB-C port —
confirm with a meter before soldering
Two 220 kΩ in series from BAT+ to GND; the midpoint feeds A0.
Halves the cell voltage (4.2 V → 2.1 V) for the ADC; reported over the BLE Battery Service.
GND = any GND pin. On a stock USB key set BATTERY_MOD 0 in the sketch.
USB-power sense (part of the battery mod)
The 5V pin (top of the right header, next to USB-C) is USB VBUS: ~5 V whenever
anything is plugged in — host, charger or power bank — and 0 V on the cell.
Same 1:1 divider as the battery one; D10 reads 2.5 V on USB.
On USB the firmware reports "level unknown" (BAT+ is the charger, not the cell)
and skips the idle sleep. Draws 11 µA, and only while USB is present.
Charge sense (optional, on top of the battery mod)
The red charge LED sits beside the USB-C jack, RESET side.
The charge IC drives it and nothing else: flashing = charging,
dark = full, solid for ~30 s after plug-in = no cell fitted.
Tap its cathode pad — the side towards the charge IC, the pad
that reads ~0 V while the LED is on — through 100 kΩ into D3.
Without this wire nothing changes: the key reports its power
state as unknown and the app shows the plain chip on USB.
